V76 LOW-LEVEL STATUS:
- New natural Level-5/10 generated records: 29
- Existing generated records broadened downward: 3
- Ordinary early sets now use natural incomplete movesets rather than artificial weak filler.
- Source-derived sets remain immutable.

RED ROGUE MOVESET CORPUS — DIFFICULTY FRAMEWORK
===================================================

IMPORTANT: CURRENT RATINGS ARE PROVISIONAL
------------------------------------------
The existing HARD / ELITE / NORMAL / EASY / BAD labels were built from several
different passes and should NOT be treated as a single precise difficulty truth.

From this version forward, difficulty should be understood on FOUR SEPARATE AXES:

1. SOURCE / COMPETITIVE QUALITY
   How strong is this set in the context it came from?
   - ELITE_SOURCE: tournament, established Smogon/community standard, serious sample team,
     or other clearly optimized competitive build.
   - STRONG_SOURCE: competitive but somewhat specialized / format-limited / imperfect.
   - SOURCE_DEFINED: official rental or historical set whose quality should be assessed
     separately from provenance.
   - PROJECT_ORIGINAL: no source-strength prior; must be evaluated directly.

   IMPORTANT:
   Smogon/community sets should receive a HIGH PRIOR by default. A standard competitive
   set should normally begin at HARD/ELITE quality, not NORMAL, unless there is a concrete
   reason to downgrade it for its actual format or implementation.

2. SET STRATEGIC QUALITY
   How coherent and effective are the four moves for this species?
   Consider:
   - STAB / coverage
   - sleep / paralysis / trapping / recovery
   - setup synergy
   - explosion / sacrifice utility
   - physical-special fit in RBY
   - redundant or dead moves
   - species stats and typing

3. LEVEL-RELATIVE THREAT
   This is separate from absolute set quality and MUST be evaluated at the target level.

   Fixed-damage examples:
   - DRAGON_RAGE always deals 40 HP. At very low levels this can be effectively a one-hit
     knockout against many Pokémon and should receive a major early-level threat premium.
   - SONICBOOM always deals 20 HP and is similarly dangerous at very low levels.
   - SEISMIC_TOSS and NIGHT_SHADE deal damage equal to the user's level, so their practical
     strength changes with level and opposing HP totals.

   Other level-sensitive effects include:
   - early sleep access
   - partial trapping against low-speed opponents
   - early high-crit moves
   - unusually early strong STAB
   - evolved stats appearing earlier/later than normal

   Therefore:
   THE SAME FOUR-MOVE SET MAY HAVE DIFFERENT TRAINER DIFFICULTY AT LEVEL 15, 30, 40, OR 55.

4. FINAL TRAINER DIFFICULTY
   Final runtime difficulty should combine:
   SOURCE QUALITY PRIOR
   + SET STRATEGIC QUALITY
   + SPECIES POWER
   + LEVEL-RELATIVE THREAT
   + ROLE/SYNERGY MODIFIERS

   Suggested output remains:
   BAD / EASY / NORMAL / HARD / ELITE

   But the final label should always be tied to a TARGET LEVEL or LEVEL BAND when possible.

SOURCE IMMUTABILITY RULE
------------------------
Externally sourced movesets are immutable:
- Stadium rentals
- player teams
- tournament teams
- historical builds
- Smogon/community sets
- RMTs
- sample teams
- other documented source builds

Their FOUR MOVES are never changed for balancing.
Their DIFFICULTY METADATA may be reassessed if the earlier rating was wrong.
Project-original / generated / retrofit sets may be edited for balance and variety.

KNOWN CURRENT RATING WEAKNESSES
-------------------------------
- Many Smogon/community sets are currently merely HARD even though they should generally
  receive an ELITE competitive-quality prior.
- Current ratings are not consistently level-relative.
- Fixed-damage moves are not yet weighted strongly enough by target level.
- Some project-original ratings were inherited from generic move-value heuristics rather
  than a full species + level matchup model.

NO RATINGS ARE CHANGED IN THIS VERSION.
This header documents the corrected framework and the accompanying audits identify where
rerating should begin.

===============================================================================
V75 — GENERATED LOW-LEVEL DIFFICULTY DIAGNOSTIC
===============================================================================

No movesets or ratings were changed in V75.

Corpus gap discovered:
- generated Level-5 curated sets: 0
- generated Level-10 curated sets: 0
- generated Level-15 curated sets: 101

The Level-15 generated layer currently diagnoses as:
BAD 2 / EASY 3 / NORMAL 41 / HARD 44 / ELITE 11.

This distribution is NOT being normalized downward. It reflects that the Level-15
curated sets often have four deliberately selected legal moves, including TMs/status/
coverage, and therefore are much stronger than natural early-route learnsets.

Future early-route generation should create genuine Level-5/10 sets with incomplete
movesets and natural early learnsets. Difficulty should emerge from those constraints,
not from an imposed rating curve.

===============================================================================


============================================================================
EXPANDED RBY FORMAT AUDIT TARGETS (Smogon / @pkmn set index)
============================================================================

The maintained Smogon-derived set index currently exposes the following
Generation 1 set datasets. A genuinely exhaustive pass should check ALL of
these, not just the standard tier sets:

- gen11v1              = 1v1
- gen1lc               = Little Cup
- gen1lclevel100       = Little Cup Level 100
- gen1middlecup        = Middle Cup
- gen1monotype         = Monotype
- gen1nc1997           = Nintendo Cup 1997
- gen1nc1999           = Nintendo Cup 1999
- gen1nu               = NU
- gen1ou               = OU
- gen1petitcup         = Petit Cup
- gen1pikacup          = Pika Cup
- gen1pu               = PU
- gen1stabmons         = STABmons
- gen1stadiumou        = Stadium OU
- gen1tradebacksou     = Tradebacks OU
- gen1ubers            = Ubers
- gen1uu               = UU
- gen1zu               = ZU

In addition, individual Smogon RBY Pokémon pages may expose fixed historical
rental sets such as Poke Cup Rentals. These must also be included when present.

Alternative/slashed moves:
When a source gives one or more alternatives in a slot, each strategically
meaningful legal combination should be represented as its own concrete
four-move entry. Do not leave the slash only in prose.

STATUS NOTE

This revision is intentionally broader than the original 336-record backbone,
but it should still be treated as a BEST-EFFORT REFERENCE rather than a claim
that every current Smogon side-format record has been captured. The audit
target above is the checklist to use for true completeness.



RED ROGUE — GENERATION 1 MOVESET REFERENCE
========================================================================

Purpose: a practical moveset list for building Red Rogue trainer data.
Runtime format follows the existing five-byte pattern:
    db POKEMON, MOVE_1, MOVE_2, MOVE_3, MOVE_4

BASE SOURCE:
Smogon damage-calc pinned Gen 1 dataset:
https://github.com/smogon/damage-calc/blob/2c50a89d9e369289965b1448a6f5c1b7d41520c7/src/js/data/sets/gen1.js

ADDITIONAL SOURCE:
Smogon RBY Strategy Dex: https://www.smogon.com/dex/rb/pokemon/

RED ROGUE FORMAT REFERENCE:
https://github.com/JSsixtyfour/redrogue/blob/404693cd24fd1a8db727e5bb3ecff60fc660e658/data/trainers/gambler_movesets.asm#L2

NOTES:
- If no source level was listed, the requested note is used exactly:
  "presume 55, no level listed"
- Tradebacks sets remain explicitly labeled Tradebacks.
- NO_MOVE is used only as a visible placeholder where the source/limited movepool
  does not provide four meaningful moves. Verify the actual Red Rogue empty-move constant.
- Supplemental entries are explicitly labeled and should be legality-checked against
  Red Rogue's current learnsets before implementation.
- Constants are normalized to Red/pret-style names where obvious; verify unusual
  constants against the repo before committing.

TOTAL SET RECORDS IN THIS DOCUMENT: 336
POKEMON WITH AT LEAST ONE RECORD: 151 / 151

CURATED SAMPLE-TEAM / RESOURCE-HUB ADDITIONS

Generation 1 resource hubs and sample-team discussions, beyond the Strategy
Dex / damage-calc backbone.

SOURCE INVENTORY USED FOR THIS PASS
-----------------------------------
- Smogon RBY Resource Hub
  Covers OU, UU, NU, Ubers, Tradebacks OU, Stadium OU, tournament archives,
  usage stats, mechanics, and links to sample teams.

- Smogon RBY OU Sample Teams
  Curated sample teams reviewed periodically to reflect metagame changes.

- Smogon RBY UU Resources
  Includes sample teams and Smogon Dex links.

- Smogon RBY NU Resources
  Includes viability rankings and sample teams.

- Smogon RBY PU Hub
  Includes current and archived sample-team collections.

- Smogon RBY ZU Hub
  Includes current/historical sample teams and concrete movesets in thread text.

- Smogon RBY Other Metas Hub
  Includes 1v1 sample teams and condensed/extended set compendia.

- Smogon RBY Tradebacks OU Hub
  Includes sample sets and sample teams.

- Smogon Master List of PS! Sample Teams
  Cross-checks the existence of sample-team resources for Gen 1 Ubers, UU,
  NU, PU, LC, 1v1, Stadium OU, Tradebacks OU, and Nintendo Cup 1997.

============================================================================
IMPORTANT DEDUPLICATION NOTE
============================================================================

Some sample-team movesets are identical to existing Smogon Strategy Dex or
damage-calc records. Those should not necessarily become duplicate runtime
entries. Instead, preserve the extra provenance in documentation.

Examples from this pass that overlap existing records include combinations
such as:
- SANDSLASH: SWORDS_DANCE / EARTHQUAKE / ROCK_SLIDE / SUBSTITUTE
- ABRA: PSYCHIC / THUNDER_WAVE / SEISMIC_TOSS / SUBSTITUTE

Those combinations are still valuable because actual team usage corroborates
the set, but a future generator should merge provenance rather than emit
duplicate five-byte records.

============================================================================
NEXT HIGH-VALUE SOURCES TO MINE
============================================================================

1. OU curated sample teams
2. UU curated sample teams
3. NU curated sample teams
4. Ubers sample teams
5. Tradebacks OU sample teams
6. Stadium OU sample teams
7. 1v1 condensed + extended set compendia
8. LC sample teams
9. PU current + archived samples
10. Major tournament team dumps / usage archives
11. Nintendo Cup 1997/1999 resources
12. Historical Pika Cup / Petit Cup / Middle Cup resources

The strategy should remain:
- prefer curated/official samples;
- add only genuinely new four-move combinations;
- preserve source provenance when a combination duplicates an existing set;
- keep historical / rental / side-format legality labels explicit.




============================================================================
V4 — CORPUS EXPANSION FOR TRAINER DIFFICULTY
============================================================================

Collection philosophy for Red Rogue:
- DO NOT filter only for optimal competitive sets.
- Keep strong, average, questionable, gimmicky, historical, rental, beginner,
  and outright bad builds when they are genuinely Gen 1 / RBY relevant.
- Random one-off tournament or RMT sets are valid data.
- The goal is a broad moveset corpus suitable for trainers of different
  difficulty levels, not a single list of "best" sets.

ROUGH QUALITY TAGS
------------------
ELITE      Highly optimized / top-end set; useful for bosses and hard trainers.
STRONG     Clearly effective, broadly coherent competitive set.
SOLID      Good but not necessarily best-in-slot or universally optimal.
MEDIOCRE   Playable but compromised, dated, narrow, or less efficient.
GIMMICK    Specialized, matchup-dependent, unusual, or deliberately tricky.
BAD        Weak, dubious, historically criticized, or useful mainly as low-difficulty data.

These labels are intentionally rough. They describe moveset quality, not the
base strength of the Pokémon species itself.

This V4 pass specifically adds:
1. RBY 1v1 Condensed Set Compendium entries.
2. Concrete variants expanded from the RBY 1v1 Extended Set Compendium.
3. Older/beginner Smogon RMT one-offs, including imperfect sets.
4. Additional Ubers sample-team variants.
5. Automatic exact-combination deduplication against V3.

============================================================================
V4 PASS SUMMARY
============================================================================
Candidate records reviewed in this pass: 63
New unique four-move combinations appended: 59
Exact combinations already present and skipped: 4

Duplicates were skipped only when the Pokémon and all four moves matched
an existing record exactly. One-move differences are retained.

The source/quality metadata for duplicate combinations may still be useful
later if this text corpus is normalized into JSON or another database.


============================================================================
V5 — RENTALS, HISTORICAL ODDITIES, AND EXPLICIT ALTERNATIVES
============================================================================

This pass intentionally targets the weak/mediocre/gimmick end of the corpus.

COLLECTION RULE CHANGE
----------------------
A moveset does NOT need to be good to be retained.

Useful source material includes:
- fixed Pokemon Stadium rentals;
- Japanese Stadium / Nintendo Cup rentals;
- old RMT one-offs;
- tournament experiments;
- explicit slashed alternatives in Smogon analyses;
- historical side-format sets;
- incomplete movepools, where applicable.

These are valuable because Red Rogue needs different trainer difficulties.

Rental sets are especially useful: Smogon's rental-format documentation
explicitly notes that fixed rentals force many Pokemon into less-than-optimal
movesets. Those sets are preserved exactly rather than "fixed."

QUALITY TAGS remain rough:
ELITE / STRONG / SOLID / MEDIOCRE / GIMMICK / BAD

============================================================================
V23 — NORMALIZED ATTRIBUTION / LOSS-MESSAGE METADATA
============================================================================

PURPOSE
-------
Every moveset should carry enough provenance to generate player-facing flavor
text after a loss, win, encounter, trainer reveal, debug screen, etc.

Examples:
    "You lost to crazyguy100's Invitational team."
    "That trainer used a Poké Cup rental set."
    "You were beaten by a Nintendo Cup '98 rental build."
    "That set came from an RBY UU sample team."
    "You lost to a weird tournament one-off from RBY Invitational VI."

The existing Source / Format / Quality comments remain useful, but future data
normalization should add the following explicit fields:

    Attribution Type:
    Attribution Name:
    Attribution Event:
    Attribution Format:
    Attribution Detail:
    Suggested Loss Text:

RECOMMENDED ATTRIBUTION TYPES
-----------------------------
COMPETITIVE_STANDARD
    Formal Smogon Strategy Dex / damage-calc set.

SAMPLE_TEAM
    Curated sample team or sample-team Poképaste.

TOURNAMENT_PLAYER
    Exact set from a named player's tournament team or dump.

TOURNAMENT_EVENT
    Tournament set where the event is known but player attribution is not.

RMT
    Rate My Team / personal team post.

RENTAL
    Fixed official rental set from Stadium / Nintendo Cup / related format.

HISTORICAL_GUIDE
    Historical competitive guide or archive.

SIDE_FORMAT
    Pika Cup, Petit Cup, Middle Cup, LC100, Monotype, STABmons, etc.

COMMUNITY_ONE_OFF
    Sourced one-off community build that is not necessarily recommended.

RED_ROGUE_SUPPLEMENTAL
    Original Red Rogue-created set.

ATTRIBUTION NORMALIZATION EXAMPLES
----------------------------------

; Example — official rental
; Attribution Type: RENTAL
; Attribution Name: Poké Cup Rental
; Attribution Event: Pokémon Stadium
; Attribution Format: Poké Cup
; Attribution Detail: Fixed Level 50 rental
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to a Poké Cup rental set.

; Example — Nintendo Cup rental
; Attribution Type: RENTAL
; Attribution Name: Nintendo Cup '98 Rental
; Attribution Event: Japanese Pokémon Stadium
; Attribution Format: Nintendo Cup 1998
; Attribution Detail: Fixed Level 30 rental
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to a Nintendo Cup '98 rental build.

; Example — curated sample team
; Attribution Type: SAMPLE_TEAM
; Attribution Name: RBY UU Sample Team
; Attribution Event: Smogon RBY UU Circuit
; Attribution Format: RBY UU
; Attribution Detail: Curated sample-team import
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to an RBY UU sample-team set.

; Example — named tournament player
; Attribution Type: TOURNAMENT_PLAYER
; Attribution Name: crazyguy100
; Attribution Event: RBY Invitational VI
; Attribution Format: RBY OU
; Attribution Detail: Exact four-move set from tournament team dump
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to crazyguy100's Invitational team.

; Example — tournament event without known player
; Attribution Type: TOURNAMENT_EVENT
; Attribution Name: RBY Invitational II
; Attribution Event: RBY Invitational II
; Attribution Format: RBY OU
; Attribution Detail: Exact tournament team / set dump
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to an RBY Invitational II tournament set.

; Example — historical RMT
; Attribution Type: RMT
; Attribution Name: Withdraw Slowbro
; Attribution Event: Smogon RMT
; Attribution Format: RBY OU
; Attribution Detail: Historical one-off team
; Suggested Loss Text: You lost to a historical RBY team build.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE
-----------------------
Do NOT use the raw Source string directly as player-facing text.

Instead normalize each record into short machine-readable attribution fields.
This makes it possible to create different flavor-text styles later.

Suggested normalized record:

    {
        species: SNORLAX,
        moves: [BODY_SLAM, REFLECT, HYPER_BEAM, REST],
        format: "RBY OU",
        quality: "STRONG",

        attribution_type: "TOURNAMENT_PLAYER",
        attribution_name: "playername",
        attribution_event: "RBY Invitational VI",
        attribution_detail: "Exact tournament team dump",

        suggested_loss_text:
            "You lost to playername's Invitational team."
    }

PLAYER NAME RULE
----------------
If the original source provides a clearly identifiable team author/player name,
preserve it exactly in Attribution Name.

Do NOT invent usernames.

If the set came from a paste/thread but no reliable player/author is identifiable,
use the event/source rather than guessing:

    "You lost to an RBY Invitational set."

instead of:

    "You lost to <invented username>."

RENTAL MESSAGE RULE
-------------------
Rental sets should normally identify the format, not an author:

    Poké Cup:
        "You lost to a Poké Cup rental set."

    Prime Cup:
        "You lost to a Prime Cup rental set."

    Petit Cup:
        "You lost to a Petit Cup rental set."

    Pika Cup:
        "You lost to a Pika Cup rental set."

    Gym Leader Castle:
        "You lost to a Gym Leader Castle rental set."

    Nintendo Cup '97:
        "You lost to a Nintendo Cup '97 rental set."

    Nintendo Cup '98:
        "You lost to a Nintendo Cup '98 rental set."

    Nintendo Cup '99:
        "You lost to a Nintendo Cup '99 rental set."

QUALITY CAN ALSO AFFECT FLAVOR
------------------------------
Optional future flavor text can combine provenance + quality:

ELITE:
    "You were crushed by a tournament-tested set from <source>."

STRONG:
    "That trainer used a proven <format> set."

SOLID:
    "You lost to a solid <format> build."

MEDIOCRE:
    "You somehow lost to a pretty ordinary <format> set."

GIMMICK:
    "You got caught by a weird <source> gimmick."

BAD:
    "You lost to a notoriously questionable <format> build."

This should be treated as optional flavor. The raw quality label should never
be shown if it would make the game feel insulting or repetitive.

IMPORTANT
---------
The corpus should preserve BOTH:
1. machine-readable normalized attribution, and
2. the full original source string / URL or source description.

The short attribution exists for gameplay flavor.
The full source exists for verification, debugging, credits, and research.

V26 — EXPANDED PROJECT SCOPE: JOHTO + KANTO-FAMILY RETROFITS
============================================================================

PROJECT SCOPE UPDATE
--------------------
The Red Rogue moveset corpus is no longer limited to the original 151 species.

It must also include:

1. ALL JOHTO POKÉMON used by Red Rogue.

2. LATER EVOLUTIONS / PRE-EVOLUTIONS OF KANTO POKÉMON used by Red Rogue.
   Examples may include species such as:
   - Pichu
   - Crobat
   - Bellossom
   - Politoed
   - Slowking
   - Steelix
   - Scizor
   - Kingdra
   and any other Kanto-family additions actually present in the hack.

3. REGIONAL VARIANTS OF KANTO POKÉMON used by Red Rogue.
   This can include Alolan, Galarian, Hisuian, or other regional forms where
   Red Rogue includes them.

4. ANY OTHER RED ROGUE SPECIES THAT BELONGS TO A KANTO EVOLUTIONARY FAMILY.

CORE COMPATIBILITY RULE
-----------------------
Red Rogue does NOT gain later-generation moves or later-generation types merely
because a later Pokémon is included.

All constructed movesets for these species must operate inside Red Rogue's
existing Gen 1-compatible battle rules.

Therefore:

- Do NOT add later-generation moves solely to support a later species.
- Do NOT assume later-generation types such as Dark, Steel, Fairy, etc. exist.
- Use the type assignment actually present in Red Rogue.
- Use only moves that exist in Red Rogue's current move table.
- Do not assume abilities, held items, natures, modern mechanics, or later
  battle-system features.

RETROFIT SET PHILOSOPHY
-----------------------
Later species should receive "Gen 1 retrofit" movesets.

These are NOT claimed to be historical RBY sets.

Their purpose is to preserve as much as possible of the species' intended
identity using the Red Rogue / Gen 1 toolset.

Evidence priority:

1. EVOLUTIONARY-FAMILY INHERITANCE
   Moves already associated with the Kanto member(s) of the same family are
   strong candidates.

2. LATER CANONICAL LEARNSETS USING GEN 1 MOVES
   If the later species canonically learns a move that already exists in
   Red Rogue / Gen 1, it may be considered.

3. ROLE PRESERVATION
   Use Gen 1 moves that preserve the broad role of the later Pokémon:
   - physical sweeper
   - special attacker
   - paralysis support
   - sleep user
   - setup sweeper
   - bulky rest user
   - mixed attacker
   - explosion/self-destruct lure
   - partial trapping user
   - gimmick / novelty build
   etc.

4. FAMILY / STAT / ROLE CONSISTENCY
   Do not give moves merely because they are strong.
   The set should still feel like the species.

QUALITY DISTRIBUTION
--------------------
Do NOT create only optimal retrofit sets.

Where movepool depth permits, create multiple quality levels:

    ELITE
    STRONG
    SOLID
    MEDIOCRE
    GIMMICK
    BAD

This remains important because Red Rogue trainer difficulty should be able to
draw from different-quality movesets.

RETROFIT ATTRIBUTION
--------------------
All constructed later-species sets must be clearly distinguishable from
historically sourced RBY material.

Recommended fields:

    Attribution Type: RED_ROGUE_RETROFIT
    Attribution Name: Red Rogue Gen 1 Retrofit
    Attribution Event: Red Rogue
    Attribution Format: Red Rogue
    Attribution Detail: Later species adapted to Red Rogue's Gen 1 move/type system
    Suggested Loss Text: You lost to a Red Rogue original set.

Where useful, the Detail field may explain the inspiration:

    Attribution Detail:
    Johto evolution of Golbat; moves selected from family inheritance and
    later canonical Gen 1-compatible learnset.

SOURCE / EVIDENCE DOCUMENTATION
-------------------------------
Each retrofit set should ideally document the evidence used:

    Retrofit Evidence:
    - Family: GOLBAT
    - Later canonical Gen 1-compatible moves: <list>
    - Intended role: fast disruptive attacker
    - Red Rogue type assignment: <type>
    - Red Rogue move availability verified: YES/NO

This evidence is research/debug metadata, not necessarily runtime data.

TYPE HANDLING
-------------
Set quality must be judged against RED ROGUE'S type assignment.

Examples:

- If a species is Steel in modern games but Red Rogue has no Steel type,
  do NOT evaluate its set as though Steel STAB exists.

- If a regional form normally gains Dark or Fairy typing but those types are
  absent from Red Rogue, use whatever type Red Rogue assigns instead.

- If Red Rogue has explicitly remapped such a form to an existing Gen 1 type,
  all STAB / weakness / role reasoning should use that remapped type.

MOVELIST VALIDATION
-------------------
Before a retrofit set is implementation-ready, every move constant must be
verified against Red Rogue's actual move table.

The corpus may temporarily contain a candidate retrofit set while research is
ongoing, but it should be marked:

    Move Validation: PENDING

or:

    Move Validation: VERIFIED

Do not silently introduce unsupported move constants.

SPECIES COVERAGE TARGET
-----------------------
The final corpus should have:

- full original Kanto coverage
- full Johto coverage for species present in Red Rogue
- full regional-form coverage for forms present in Red Rogue
- full later Kanto-family evolution/pre-evolution coverage
- multiple sets per species wherever the movepool supports meaningful variety

SOURCED VS CONSTRUCTED DATA
---------------------------
The corpus now has two major classes:

A. HISTORICAL / SOURCED
   - Smogon analyses
   - sample teams
   - tournament dumps
   - RMTs
   - official Stadium rentals
   - Nintendo Cup rentals
   - historical guides
   - side formats

B. RED ROGUE RETROFIT
   - Johto species
   - regional Kanto forms
   - later Kanto-family species
   - any other non-RBY species in Red Rogue

Never blur the distinction between these classes.

A retrofit may be inspired by later competitive history, but the resulting
four-move combination is still a RED_ROGUE_RETROFIT unless it is directly
documented in an actual Gen 1-compatible metagame/source.

LOSS-MESSAGE BEHAVIOR
---------------------
Historical sourced set:
    "You lost to Amaranth's Global Championships team."
    "You lost to a Poké Cup rental set."

Constructed retrofit:
    "You lost to a Red Rogue original set."

Optional species-specific flavor could later be layered on top, but provenance
must remain accurate.

UPDATED NEXT-STAGE WORK PLAN
----------------------------
1. Continue tournament / archive mining:
   - Invitational III / IV
   - remaining RBY Cup X sets
   - SPL / World Cup archives
   - additional Ubers dumps
   - RMT archives

2. Audit Red Rogue's actual expanded species roster.

3. Audit Red Rogue's actual type assignments for later species/forms.

4. Audit Red Rogue's move table / allowed move constants.

5. Build a retrofit evidence table:
   species -> family -> Red Rogue type -> legal Gen 1-compatible moves -> roles.

6. Generate multiple retrofit sets per eligible species.

7. Preserve provenance / quality / level / format metadata exactly as with the
   historical corpus.

V28 — SOURCE-AUTHOR DISTINCTION + INVITATIONAL IV NAILS SETS
============================================================================


PROVENANCE FIELD CLARIFICATION
------------------------------
For all future ingested sets, distinguish:

    Attribution Name:
        The player/team owner whose set this was.

    Source Author:
        The person who posted, documented, analyzed, or archived the set.

These may be the same person, as with phoopes' Invitational IV posts:
    Attribution Name: phoopes
    Source Author: phoopes

They may also differ:
    Attribution Name: Nails
    Source Author: event-thread analysis contributor

The gameplay loss message should normally use Attribution Name, NOT Source Author.

Examples:
    "You lost to phoopes' Invitational IV team."
    "You lost to Nails' Invitational IV set."

If the actual player is unknown but the source author is known, do not falsely
treat the poster as the player. Use event-level attribution instead.

Example:
    Attribution Type: TOURNAMENT_EVENT
    Attribution Name: RBY Invitational IV
    Source Author: <poster>
    Suggested Loss Text: You lost to an Invitational IV tournament set.

============================================================================
V32 — RED ROGUE RETROFIT PHASE: REPOSITORY AUDIT + FIRST CANDIDATES
============================================================================

PUBLIC-REPOSITORY AUDIT
-----------------------
The currently public Red Rogue master branch was audited before generating
expanded-roster movesets.

Findings:

1. The public species constant table is still the original Kanto species table.
2. data/pokemon/base_stats.asm still includes the original Kanto base-stat files.
3. The public move constant table remains the Gen 1 move list, with ROAR
   repurposed as SUPER_TRANSFORM.
4. Newer systems such as fusion and special/type variants are present, but
   they operate on the existing species structures rather than exposing a
   public Johto species table.

CONSEQUENCE
-----------
Johto / regional / later-family sets can now be DESIGNED, but they cannot yet
be marked implementation-verified against the public master branch.

Until the expanded roster branch/local project data is available, these records
must use:

    Roster Validation: PENDING
    Type Validation: PENDING
    Move Validation: CANDIDATE

No later-generation move constant is introduced.

============================================================================
V33 — EXPANDED TYPE REMAPS + LEVEL-LEGAL / DIFFICULTY-STRATIFIED SET SYSTEM
============================================================================

EXPANDED-ROSTER TYPE REMAP RULES
--------------------------------
Until Red Rogue's expanded roster implementation is finalized, use these design
rules for later-generation types:

PRIMARY DARK
    -> NORMAL

PRIMARY FAIRY
    -> NORMAL

SECONDARY DARK
    -> REMOVE SECONDARY TYPE

SECONDARY STEEL
    -> REMOVE SECONDARY TYPE

SECONDARY FAIRY
    -> REMOVE SECONDARY TYPE

PRIMARY STEEL
    -> ROCK

Examples of how this should be interpreted conceptually:

    UMBREON
        modern primary Dark
        -> Red Rogue Normal

    CLEFFA / TOGEPI / SNUBBULL families where Fairy is primary in modern data
        -> Red Rogue Normal

    SCIZOR
        modern Bug / Steel
        -> Red Rogue Bug
        Steel secondary is removed

    MAGNEMITE / MAGNETON style Electric / Steel
        -> Red Rogue Electric
        Steel secondary is removed

    STEELIX
        modern Steel / Ground
        -> Red Rogue Rock / Ground
        Steel primary becomes Rock

    SKARMORY
        modern Steel / Flying
        -> Red Rogue Rock / Flying
        Steel primary becomes Rock

These remaps are design rules for retrofit reasoning. Final implementation
must still use the actual Red Rogue species data once the expanded roster lands.

============================================================================
LEVEL LEGALITY AND DIFFICULTY ARE SEPARATE AXES
============================================================================

The corpus should no longer assume one generic moveset per Pokémon.

Every species should be capable of having sets indexed by:

    SPECIES
    TARGET LEVEL
    DIFFICULTY / QUALITY
    FORMAT / SOURCE
    MOVE-ACQUISITION POLICY

A useful conceptual key is:

    (species, target_level, difficulty_tier, acquisition_policy)

Example:

    PIDGEOTTO, Level 15, EASY, NATURAL
    PIDGEOTTO, Level 15, HARD, FULL_LEGAL
    PIDGEOTTO, Level 20, EASY, NATURAL
    PIDGEOTTO, Level 20, HARD, FULL_LEGAL

These are distinct records.

============================================================================
MOVE-ACQUISITION POLICIES
============================================================================

NATURAL
    Only moves naturally available by the target level through the intended
    level-up/evolution rules.

TRAINER_NORMAL
    Natural level-up moves plus a conservative amount of plausible TM/HM use.

FULL_LEGAL
    Any move legally available to that species in Red Rogue by the target
    level, including legal TM/HM/tutor-equivalent sources supported by the hack.

SPECIAL_SOURCE
    Official rental / event / historical set that intentionally violates the
    normal progression assumptions or comes from a fixed source.

RED_ROGUE_CURATED
    Explicitly curated trainer set. Must still use supported moves, but may use
    deliberate TM-heavy combinations appropriate to trainer difficulty.

============================================================================
LEVEL-LEGAL MOVE RULE
============================================================================

For a target Level L:

1. Include all level-up moves learned at or before Level L.

2. Include inherited/evolution moves only if Red Rogue actually permits them
   for that species/set-generation path.

3. TM/HM moves are NOT automatically excluded just because the Pokémon is low
   level. If the species can legally learn the TM/HM and the selected
   acquisition policy permits TMs/HMs, the move may appear at Level L.

4. Do not include a later level-up move merely because it is part of the
   species' eventual movepool.

5. Species evolution-level legality should be tracked separately from move
   legality.

This distinction is important for trainer Pokémon.

A Level-15 Pidgeotto can be treated as a valid trainer Pokémon if Red Rogue
allows underleveled evolved species, while its natural move pool should still
be evaluated at Level 15.

============================================================================
SPECIES-LEVEL LEGALITY VS MOVE-LEVEL LEGALITY
============================================================================

Track these independently:

    Species Level Status:
        NORMAL
        UNDERSLEVELED_EVOLUTION
        FIXED_RENTAL
        SPECIAL_TRAINER
        UNKNOWN

    Move Legality:
        VERIFIED
        CANDIDATE
        INVALID

Example:

    PIDGEOTTO at Level 15

Pidgeotto normally evolves from Pidgey later than Level 15 in standard RBY,
but Red Rogue may still intentionally place a Level-15 Pidgeotto on a trainer.

That record can therefore be:

    Species Level Status: UNDERLEVELED_EVOLUTION
    Move Legality: VERIFIED

This is much better than rejecting the entire moveset merely because the
evolution level is unusual.

============================================================================
DIFFICULTY TIERS
============================================================================

Difficulty should affect move QUALITY, not raw legality.

Suggested runtime difficulty categories:

EASY
    - mostly level-up moves
    - redundant coverage allowed
    - weak/status moves allowed
    - little or no optimized TM use
    - poor synergy is acceptable

NORMAL
    - coherent STAB / coverage
    - perhaps one useful TM
    - basic status support
    - avoids obviously terrible combinations

HARD
    - strong legal coverage
    - synergistic status/setup
    - strategic TM/HM use
    - few wasted slots

ELITE
    - best or near-best legal set for the target level
    - aggressive TM/HM access where legal
    - tuned coverage and synergy
    - may resemble competitive sets when the level permits

GIMMICK
    - coherent but unusual strategy
    - intentionally weird tech
    - may be stronger or weaker than NORMAL depending on matchup

BAD
    - intentionally poor set for low-difficulty / comedic / historical use
    - must still be legal unless explicitly tagged otherwise

The existing corpus quality labels:

    ELITE
    STRONG
    SOLID
    MEDIOCRE
    GIMMICK
    BAD

can map onto runtime difficulty without losing historical/source metadata.

============================================================================
EXAMPLE: PIDGEOTTO LEVEL STRATIFICATION
============================================================================

Generation-I reference:
Pidgeotto naturally has access by Level 15 to:
    GUST
    SAND_ATTACK
    QUICK_ATTACK

WHIRLWIND is learned later at Level 21.
WING_ATTACK is learned later at Level 31.

Pidgeotto is also compatible with several Gen-1 TMs/HMs such as:
    FLY
    RAZOR_WIND
    TOXIC
    TAKE_DOWN
    DOUBLE_EDGE
    RAGE
    MIMIC
    DOUBLE_TEAM
    REFLECT
    BIDE
    SWIFT
    SKY_ATTACK
    REST
    SUBSTITUTE

Therefore Level 15 can legitimately support very different difficulty sets,
depending on acquisition policy.

At Level 21+, WHIRLWIND can enter natural-level sets.
At Level 31+, WING_ATTACK can enter natural-level sets.
At Level 40+, AGILITY can enter natural-level sets.

This means the generator should derive candidate sets from the exact target
level rather than simply choosing from one species-wide pool.

============================================================================
RECOMMENDED DATA MODEL
============================================================================

A future normalized moveset record should contain at least:

    species
    moves[4]

    minimum_level
    target_level
    maximum_level_optional

    difficulty
    quality

    acquisition_policy

    species_level_status
    move_legality

    format
    source
    attribution_type
    attribution_name
    source_author
    attribution_event

    retrofit_type_1
    retrofit_type_2

    notes

Example conceptual record:

    {
        species: PIDGEOTTO,
        target_level: 15,
        difficulty: HARD,
        acquisition_policy: FULL_LEGAL,

        moves: [
            FLY,
            DOUBLE_EDGE,
            QUICK_ATTACK,
            REFLECT
        ],

        species_level_status: UNDERLEVELED_EVOLUTION,
        move_legality: VERIFIED,

        quality: STRONG
    }

============================================================================
GENERATOR ARCHITECTURE IMPLICATION
============================================================================

The eventual moveset generator should NOT store every possible level manually.

Prefer:

1. Species legal-move data with acquisition metadata:
       move
       source
       learn_level
       TM/HM status
       inherited status

2. Difficulty rules.

3. Curated historical / rental / retrofit templates.

Then generate or validate level-specific sets programmatically.

The corpus can still preserve hand-authored sets where they matter.

Conceptually:

    legal_moves = get_legal_moves(species, level, acquisition_policy)

    candidate_sets = historical_sets
                   + curated_sets
                   + generated_combinations(legal_moves)

    filtered_sets = filter_by_difficulty(candidate_sets, difficulty)

This allows one balancing script to ask:

    "Give me a Level-15 Pidgeotto for an EASY trainer."

or:

    "Give me a Level-20 Pidgeotto for an ELITE trainer."

without maintaining thousands of near-duplicate hardcoded records.

============================================================================
NEXT PHASE
============================================================================

1. Continue Johto / expanded-roster candidate construction.
2. Apply the new type remap rules.
3. Begin a legal-move-by-level model for Kanto species.
4. Use Pidgeotto and several other representative species as validation cases.
5. Extend the same system to Johto retrofits once their Red Rogue learnsets are
   finalized.
6. Ultimately let the balancing/generator script choose sets by:
       species + level + difficulty + format/source constraints.
============================================================================



============================================================================
V34 — CURATED LEVEL-SET POLICY REFINEMENT
============================================================================

IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION
--------------------------
Do NOT create hand-authored movesets for every species at many arbitrary levels.

Red Rogue already has:
- natural level-based move learning
- randomized movesets
- trainer-generation systems

Therefore, the curated corpus should only create a level-specific record when
the target level creates a DISTINCT, MEANINGFUL BUILD.

LEVEL-SPECIFIC SETS SHOULD BE ADDED WHEN:
-----------------------------------------
1. A key move becomes available at that level and materially changes the set.
2. The species has a notably different low-level competitive / rental / cup set.
3. A legal TM/HM combination creates a distinctive trainer build at that level.
4. The species is underleveled-evolved and the set is intentionally designed
   around that unusual level.
5. The exact level is part of the historical source:
   - Pika Cup
   - Petit Cup
   - Nintendo Cup
   - rentals
   - LC
   - other fixed-level formats
6. A boss / gym / elite trainer needs a hand-designed level-specific set.
7. The level creates a genuinely different role:
   - pre-setup vs post-setup
   - before / after a key STAB
   - before / after sleep/paralysis access
   - before / after strong coverage
   - before / after recovery

DO NOT ADD LEVEL-SPECIFIC SETS WHEN:
-----------------------------------
- the moveset is merely the same set with one naturally learned move upgraded
- the game's normal level-up logic already handles the progression adequately
- the randomized-moveset system already supplies enough variety
- the target level produces no strategically meaningful difference
- it would create large amounts of near-duplicate corpus data

PREFERRED CURATED DATA MODEL
----------------------------
Most curated records should remain level-flexible:

    species
    moves[4]
    minimum_legal_level (if meaningful)
    quality
    difficulty
    acquisition_policy
    source / provenance

Only add:

    exact_target_level

when exact level meaningfully matters.

EXAMPLE — PIDGEOTTO
-------------------
Do NOT automatically create:
    Level 15 Easy
    Level 15 Normal
    Level 15 Hard
    Level 20 Easy
    Level 20 Normal
    Level 20 Hard
    Level 25 Easy
    ...

Instead, preserve only interesting curated breakpoints.

Possible examples:

LOW-LEVEL SPECIAL TRAINER SET
    Exact Target Level: 15
    Reason:
        underleveled evolved trainer Pokémon with intentional TM access

    db PIDGEOTTO, FLY, QUICK_ATTACK, REFLECT, DOUBLE_EDGE

NATURAL MIDGAME BREAKPOINT
    Minimum Legal Level: 31
    Reason:
        WING_ATTACK becomes naturally available and creates a distinct
        non-TM Flying-STAB build

    db PIDGEOTTO, WING_ATTACK, QUICK_ATTACK, DOUBLE_EDGE, REFLECT

If neither is useful in actual trainer design, omit both and allow the natural /
randomized systems to handle Pidgeotto entirely.

DIFFICULTY STILL MATTERS
------------------------
Difficulty should still be metadata on curated sets.

Examples:

    EASY / MEDIOCRE
    NORMAL / SOLID
    HARD / STRONG
    ELITE / ELITE
    GIMMICK / GIMMICK
    BAD / BAD

But difficulty does NOT require a separate set at every level.

The generator may choose:
- natural moves
- randomized moves
- curated corpus sets

based on trainer difficulty.

RECOMMENDED RUNTIME SELECTION MODEL
-----------------------------------
Conceptually:

    if special_curated_set_exists(species, level, difficulty):
        use curated candidate pool

    else if trainer_mode_prefers_randomized:
        use randomized moveset

    else:
        use natural level-based moves

This keeps the curated database high-signal.

============================================================================
EXPANDED-ROSTER RETROFIT IMPLICATION
============================================================================

For Johto / regional / later-family species:

1. Build several species-wide curated retrofit sets where useful.
2. Assign quality / difficulty.
3. Add minimum legal level only when a move-learning breakpoint matters.
4. Add exact target level only for genuinely level-specific builds.
5. Do not manufacture dozens of low-level variants merely for completeness.

This means the retrofit corpus can focus on:
- role diversity
- difficulty diversity
- source / inspiration diversity
- meaningful legal breakpoints

rather than exhaustive level enumeration.

============================================================================
NEXT IMPLEMENTATION DIRECTION
============================================================================

The next retrofit work should prioritize:

1. Full Johto species candidate coverage.
2. Multiple meaningful quality tiers per species where justified.
3. Regional / later-Kanto-family retrofits.
4. Type remaps from V33.
5. Minimum legal level annotations only where strategically important.
6. Exact-level records only when the exact level creates a distinct build.
7. Leave routine move progression to Red Rogue's natural-learning system.
8. Leave broad unpredictable variety to the randomized-moveset system.

============================================================================

final legality remains pending because Red Rogue's Johto expansion is still
under construction.

============================================================================
V36 — GSC SMOGON -> RED ROGUE ADAPTATION LAYER
============================================================================

PURPOSE
-------
Actual GSC Smogon sets are now used as a separate inspiration/source layer.
These are not historical RBY sets and are not treated as pure Red Rogue
originals either. They preserve a recognizable GSC strategic core while
translating later-only mechanics into Red Rogue's Gen-1 move/type system.

ADAPTATION STANDARD
-------------------
- Keep Gen-1 moves unchanged whenever possible.
- Remove items, abilities, natures, EV assumptions, and later mechanics.
- Replace later-only moves only when there is a clear role-preserving option.
- If too much of the original set must be rewritten, do NOT call it GSC-adapted;
  keep it in the normal RED_ROGUE_RETROFIT bucket instead.
- Apply Red Rogue type remaps when judging the adapted role.

============================================================================
V37 — GSC ADAPTATION PASS 2: HIGH-FIDELITY SURVIVORS
============================================================================

TRANSLATION POLICY REINFORCED
-----------------------------
Not every good GSC set deserves a RED_ROGUE_RETROFIT_GSC label.

Species such as Houndoom, Heracross, and Donphan depend heavily on moves that
do not exist in Red Rogue's Gen-1 move system (Pursuit, Crunch, Megahorn,
Rapid Spin, Sleep Talk, Curse, Protect, etc.). If translating a set destroys
most of its original strategic identity, the result belongs in the ordinary
RED_ROGUE_RETROFIT pool instead of pretending to be a faithful GSC adaptation.

Scizor is included once here as an explicit LOW-fidelity boundary example.

V38 — JOHTO ORIGINAL RETROFITS: MID/LATE ROSTER EXPANSION
============================================================================

These are deliberate Red Rogue originals for Johto species whose GSC identity
does not always survive a strict Gen-1 translation. GSC roles and canonical
movepools are used as evidence, but the sets are NOT mislabeled as historical
or high-fidelity GSC adaptations.

Type remaps applied:
- primary Dark -> Normal
- primary Fairy -> Normal
- secondary Dark / Steel / Fairy -> removed
- primary Steel -> Rock

Curated-set rule:
- no 'four most recently learned moves' snapshots
- no automatic level-by-level duplicates
- every set should represent a coherent trainer build, coverage concept, tank,
  setup plan, disruption package, or intentional gimmick

============================================================================
V39 — JOHTO ENDGAME / LEGENDARIES + FINAL CORE FAMILY ORIGINALS
============================================================================

This pass finishes the major Johto endgame species and adds a few additional
Scizor / Kingdra / Steelix originals only where they represent genuinely
different roles from earlier entries.

V40 — REGIONAL KANTO FORMS + LATER KANTO-FAMILY EXPANSION
============================================================================

IMPORTANT CLEANUP
-----------------
V38 accidentally included PRESENT on one Delibird candidate. PRESENT is a
Generation-II move and violates the project rule. In this cumulative V40
master, that line has been corrected to use MIMIC instead.

MOVE-VOCABULARY GATE
--------------------
All newly added V40 retrofit moves were checked against the Generation-I move
vocabulary before append. Species-specific legality remains pending because
the expanded Red Rogue roster/learnsets are still under construction.

Existing cumulative move tokens not recognized by the Gen-1 vocabulary audit: ['HI_JUMP_KICK']

FORM CONSTANT NOTE
------------------
Names such as RAICHU_ALOLA and MAROWAK_ALOLA are proposed corpus identifiers,
not claims about the final ASM constant spelling. They must be mapped to the
actual Red Rogue form constants when that system is finalized.

NEXT CURATION RULE
------------------
Prioritize species/forms with only 1–2 curated sets IF another genuinely
different role exists. Do not add filler merely to equalize counts.

Examples of useful gap-filling:
- offense vs support
- tank vs breaker
- setup vs immediate damage
- status/disruption vs all-out attacks
- meaningful gimmick distinct from standard set

Examples to avoid:
- cosmetic move swaps with same strategy
- four-most-recently-learned moves
- near-duplicate coverage sets
- guessed tournament filler moves

RECOMMENDED NEXT PASS
---------------------
1. Review every 1-set species/form for a second meaningful role.
2. Review every 2-set species/form only where a third role is truly distinct.
3. Normalize provenance on older records that predate the modern schema.
4. Then prepare the corpus for generator-oriented quality/difficulty balancing.

============================================================================
V46 — QUALITY / DIFFICULTY NORMALIZATION FOR TRAINER GENERATION
============================================================================

PURPOSE
-------
The historical/source-facing Quality field is preserved exactly as written.
A separate generator-facing layer is now added so trainer selection can use
consistent difficulty semantics without destroying source provenance.

NORMALIZED GENERATOR DIFFICULTY
-------------------------------
ELITE
    Near-best / boss-grade / highly optimized curated set.

HARD
    Strong competitive or tournament-grade set, but not necessarily the
    absolute best possible configuration.

NORMAL
    Coherent, useful set with reasonable synergy and coverage.

EASY
    Intentionally mediocre, weak, historical, or otherwise forgiving set.

GIMMICK
    Matchup-dependent or unusual strategy. Difficulty is not assumed merely
    from the label; gimmicks can be weak or dangerous depending on matchup.

SOURCE_DEFINED
    Fixed-source set such as an official rental. The generator should preserve
    it as a source-authentic set rather than forcing a strength judgment.

UNASSESSED
    Legacy or unusual label where no safe automatic quality judgment exists.

QUALITY -> GENERATOR MAPPING
----------------------------
ELITE      -> ELITE
STRONG     -> HARD
SOLID      -> NORMAL
MEDIOCRE   -> EASY
BAD        -> EASY
GIMMICK    -> GIMMICK
RENTAL / UNRANKED -> SOURCE_DEFINED
TOURNAMENT -> HARD
anything ambiguous -> UNASSESSED

IMPORTANT DESIGN RULES
----------------------
1. Difficulty and provenance remain separate.
   A rental can be weak or strong but should still be tagged SOURCE_DEFINED.

2. GIMMICK is not synonymous with EASY.
   A weird set may be terrible generally but lethal in one matchup.

3. Historical BAD / MEDIOCRE sets are intentionally useful.
   They should remain eligible for low-difficulty trainers.

4. Strong historical tournament sets should generally land in HARD unless
   individually curated as ELITE.

5. The generator may later assign weights inside each difficulty tier rather
   than treating all sets in a tier as equally likely.

SUGGESTED GENERATOR BEHAVIOR
----------------------------
EASY trainers:
    primarily EASY + some NORMAL + occasional harmless GIMMICK

NORMAL trainers:
    primarily NORMAL + some EASY/HARD + occasional GIMMICK

HARD trainers:
    primarily HARD + some ELITE/NORMAL + curated GIMMICK

ELITE / boss trainers:
    primarily ELITE + HARD, with only deliberate gimmicks

Rental/source-themed trainers:
    may intentionally override strength filtering and draw SOURCE_DEFINED sets
    from the correct event/format pool.

PASS SUMMARY
------------
Moveset records scanned: 1734
Records given generator-facing normalization: 1734
Records already carrying generator-facing fields: 0

Observed historical Quality labels:
- RENTAL / UNRANKED: 545
- UNLABELED: 380
- STRONG: 261
- RENTAL / UNRANKED (do not assume competitive quality): 147
- GIMMICK: 138
- SOLID: 99
- ELITE: 75
- MEDIOCRE: 44
- TOURNAMENT / UNRANKED: 30
- BAD: 15

NEXT STEP
---------
Run a targeted audit of UNASSESSED / SOURCE_DEFINED / GIMMICK records and
optionally add numeric selection weights for the actual trainer generator.

============================================================================
V47 — TARGETED UNASSESSED / SOURCE_DEFINED / GIMMICK REVIEW + WEIGHTS
============================================================================

PURPOSE
-------
Convert the broad V46 normalization into practical generator behavior.

BASE WEIGHT MODEL
-----------------
ELITE      -> 85
HARD       -> 75
NORMAL     -> 60
EASY       -> 50
GIMMICK    -> 20–35 depending on source context
SOURCE_DEFINED rental -> 100 inside its dedicated source pool
UNASSESSED legacy -> conservative 40 unless source evidence supports promotion

POOL RULES
----------
STANDARD
    Normal weighted selection.

GIMMICK_LIMITED
    Eligible only as a minority share of ordinary trainer pools unless a
    trainer/theme explicitly requests gimmicks.

SOURCE_POOL_ONLY
    Fixed-source sets such as official rentals should normally be selected
    only when the trainer/event asks for that source pool.

SOURCE_CONTEXT
    Source-authentic non-rental set; may be selected when event/source flavor
    is relevant.

LEGACY_CONSERVATIVE
    Retain but avoid overusing until provenance/quality is manually upgraded.

RECOMMENDED TRAINER MIX
-----------------------
EASY:
    65% EASY
    25% NORMAL
    10% GIMMICK/legacy

NORMAL:
    20% EASY
    55% NORMAL
    20% HARD
    5% GIMMICK

HARD:
    10% NORMAL
    65% HARD
    20% ELITE
    5% GIMMICK

ELITE/BOSS:
    25% HARD
    70% ELITE
    5% deliberate GIMMICK

IMPORTANT
---------
These percentages are generator defaults, not hard rules. Gym leaders, rivals,
themed trainers, rentals, or historical-source encounters can override them.

============================================================================
V48 — RENTAL STRATEGIC RATINGS
============================================================================

PURPOSE
-------
Official rental provenance is preserved exactly. This pass adds a separate
strategic rating so the generator can distinguish strong and weak rentals
without removing their RENTAL / SOURCE_DEFINED identity.

RATING SCALE
------------
ELITE  85–100
HARD   70–84
NORMAL 55–69
EASY   40–54
BAD     0–39

METHOD
------
- Based primarily on the Gen-1 strategic move-value table.
- Rewards recovery, useful status, and setup with compatible attacks.
- Penalizes status-heavy/no-offense structures, weak filler, and notorious
  low-value moves such as Focus Energy, Splash, Teleport, or Whirlwind.
- Does NOT alter the original rental source designation.
- Does NOT claim to be a perfect species-aware competitive rating because
  the current pass does not apply species stats, STAB, or matchup data.

Rental records rated: 710
Average strategic score: 73.7

Rating distribution:
- ELITE: 144
- HARD: 325
- NORMAL: 198
- EASY: 33
- BAD: 10

GENERATOR USAGE
---------------
Rental/source-themed encounters should still select from the appropriate
rental source pool first. Within that pool, this new rating can filter or
weight sets by trainer difficulty.

Example:
  Easy rental trainer -> mostly Rental Strategic Rating EASY/NORMAL
  Hard rental trainer -> mostly HARD, with some NORMAL/ELITE
  Rental showcase -> ignore strength rating and preserve full source pool

- setup/attack synergy
- recovery + bulk
- Explosion/Self-Destruct + Attack
- partial trapping + Speed
- mixed-offense viability

Important:
Rental provenance is NOT changed. A set remains an official rental even when

============================================================================
V54 — LEVEL RANGE / BAND LAYER
============================================================================

Every moveset now has distinct level metadata:
- Source Fixed Level
- Recommended Level Min
- Recommended Level Max
- Recommended Level Bands
- Level Range Basis
- Level Status
- Level Legality Validation

CRITICAL DISTINCTION
--------------------
A Recommended Level Range is a generator-use recommendation, NOT proof that
every move is naturally/legalistically available at every level in that range.
Exact Red Rogue learnset legality must be validated against the in-progress
expanded roster/learnsets.

HISTORICAL SOURCE LEVELS
------------------------
Fixed historical levels are preserved exactly when present (rentals, LC, etc.).

NON-FIXED SET DEFAULTS
----------------------
Sets whose source did not specify a level receive conservative starting ranges:
BAD/EASY -> 15+
NORMAL   -> 25+
HARD     -> 35+
ELITE    -> 40+

This does NOT prevent creating deliberate low-level HARD/ELITE sets. Indeed,
the existing level-15 Pika Cup pool proves that strategically strong low-level
sets can and should exist. Those should be created/validated as a dedicated
low-level curation layer rather than by falsely declaring every endgame set
legal at level 15.

CURRENT BAND AVAILABILITY (before legality filtering)
-----------------------------------------------------
- 05-14: 162 sets recommended/anchored

- 50-59: 1317 sets recommended/anchored
- 60-74: 1464 sets recommended/anchored
- 75-100: 1106 sets recommended/anchored

Fixed source-level counts:
- Level 5: 59
- Level 15: 103
- Level 20: 4
- Level 25: 72
- Level 30: 32
- Level 50: 358
- Level 100: 147

NEXT LEVEL-CURATION PASS
------------------------
1. Build deliberate level-15 curated sets beyond the existing Pika Cup pool.
2. Build level-20/25 and level-30 bands where meaningful.
3. Build level-40 sets as the major midgame competitive breakpoint.
4. Preserve level-50/55 competitive/source sets for late game.
5. Validate exact move legality against Red Rogue learnsets when available.

V55 — FIXED-LEVEL ANCHOR CLEANUP + LEVEL-15 CURATED TRANCHE 1
============================================================================

FIXED-LEVEL RANGE CLEANUP
-------------------------
Historical fixed-level sets now stay near their source level.
Notably, Level-15 Pika Cup rentals are recommended only for 15-20, not 10-20.

LEVEL-15 CURATION POLICY
------------------------
- Add deliberate early-game builds across EASY / NORMAL / HARD / ELITE.
- Do not simply truncate endgame movesets.
- Preserve meaningful strategic identity at low level.
- Exact Red Rogue legality remains PENDING until local learnsets are validated.

==============================================================================
V58 — LEVEL-15 PUBLIC-MASTER LEGALITY AUDIT + REPAIRS
==============================================================================

Scope:
- All 106 hand-curated Red Rogue Level-15 records from V55-V57.
- Historical fixed-level rentals were not rewritten; their source legality was
  already preserved separately.

Legality rule for trainer sets:
A move is accepted at Level 15 when the public Red Rogue master establishes it
through one of the following paths:
1. level-1/base learnset;
2. level-up learnset at level 15 or below;
3. explicit tutor learnset available from the species data;
4. species TM/HM compatibility (trainer-set legality, independent of when the
   player personally obtains the TM/HM);
5. retained pre-evolution move where applicable.

Important:
- This validates against the PUBLIC MASTER snapshot checked 2026-09-04.
- The user's expanded local Johto/regional roster is still under construction;
  this pass therefore applies to the Kanto Level-15 curated tranche only.
- PSYCHIC in the corpus corresponds to the repo's PSYCHIC_M move constant.

Audit totals:
- Hand-curated Level-15 records audited: 106
- Confirmed without move changes: 26
- Repaired to a confirmed-legal combination: 80
- Exact collisions with pre-existing non-Level15 corpus after repair: 0

The repaired versions now carry:
  Level Legality Validation: CONFIRMED_RED_ROGUE_PUBLIC_MASTER

Next level-specific curation should use this legality-first workflow from the
start rather than adding a PENDING set and repairing later.

============================================================================
V59 — LEGALITY-FIRST LEVEL 25 / LEVEL 30 CURATED TRANCHE 1
============================================================================

LEGALITY METHOD
---------------
Every move used in this tranche was already confirmed legal by Level 15 in V58
for the Pokémon itself or its direct pre-evolution. Evolved species are used
only when that evolution can exist by the target level.

This makes the tranche conservative but genuinely legality-confirmed.

V59 PASS SUMMARY
============================================================================
New confirmed-legal Level-25 sets: 25
New confirmed-legal Level-30 sets: 16
Total new sets: 41

Next:
- expand Level-25/30 with moves newly learned between 16-30
- then build Level-40 using exact Red Rogue learnset/TM legality from the start

============================================================================
V60 — RBY REST DE-EMPHASIS CORRECTION
============================================================================

Reason:
Earlier Johto/later-family translations over-imported GSC's Rest-heavy style.
Red Rogue does not have Sleep Talk/Snore/item wake support, so Rest is much
more costly and should not function as a generic fourth move.

Red Rogue-created/retrofit sets containing Rest before audit: 222
Rest instances removed: 202
Intentional Rest sets retained: 20
Reduction: 91.0%

Policy after V60:
- Rest is NOT generic longevity.
- Most offensive/setup/coverage sets should avoid it.
- At most one Rest-centric build is retained for most genuinely bulky species.
- Rest remains valid for specific defensive/stall concepts.
- No Sleep Talk-style assumptions are used anywhere.

Replacement policy:
- Prefer moves already used elsewhere on that same species in the Red Rogue
  corpus, reducing speculative learnset assumptions.
- Preserve exact-set duplicate policy.
- Expanded-species legality remains subject to the existing roster validation.

============================================================================
V61 — LEVEL 25/30 NEW-LEARNSET TRANCHE + POST-REST POLICY
============================================================================

These sets intentionally use moves that become available during Levels 16-30
in the current Red Rogue public master, making them strategically different
from the Level-15 pool.

All are marked CONFIRMED_RED_ROGUE_PUBLIC_MASTER with an explicit move-level
basis. Generic Rest is not used.

V64 — LEVEL 40 TRANCHE 2: ORDINARY-TRAINER COVERAGE
============================================================================

Purpose:
Balance the first Level-40 tranche by adding many NORMAL and some EASY sets,
so Level 40 does not imply boss-grade optimization.

Policy:
- no generic Rest
- no exact species + four-move duplicates
- conservative legality from previously verified species/family move pools
- evolved species used only at a plausible Level-40 stage

============================================================================
V65 — LEVEL 40 EASY/BAD CLEANUP
============================================================================

Purpose:
Add intentionally weak-but-legal Level-40 sets so ordinary trainers can still
roll mediocre or poor movesets at this stage of a run.

These are not illegal filler sets. Weakness comes from low synergy, weak moves,
redundancy, or passive choices such as Bide—not from impossible move access.

runtime corpus. Their db lines are commented out intentionally.

Cut policy:
- CUT_EXACT_DUPLICATE: same species + same four moves, ignoring move order.
  Preferred active keeper favors historical/rental/person-attributed provenance.
- CUT_REDUNDANT_REST_VARIANT: project-original Rest version shares the same
  other three moves with an equivalent non-Rest set at the same level/quality.

============================================================================
V72 — ROLE-AWARE NEAR-DUPLICATE AUDIT
============================================================================

Result:
No additional near-duplicate sets were automatically cut in this pass.

Why:
After V71 removed exact duplicates and obvious redundant Rest variants, the
remaining 3-of-4 similarities were overwhelmingly meaningful differences:
- KEEP_LEVEL_VARIANT: 177
- KEEP_DIFFICULTY_VARIANT: 100
- KEEP_DISTINCT_ROLE_OR_COVERAGE: 30
- KEEP_MEANINGFUL_ALTERNATIVE: 1

Active runtime sets remain: 1917
Cut archive sets remain: 307

Interpretation:
- Same species + 3 shared moves is not enough to justify pruning.
- Level and difficulty variants are intentionally preserved.
- Coverage differences are preserved because they produce different matchups.
- Near-equal same-role alternatives are preserved unless one is clearly redundant.
- Historical/provenance-bearing sets continue to receive a strong keep bias.

Next sensible pruning target:
Audit broader strategic repetition across project-original retrofits by role
(for example, many species repeatedly using Body Slam + Toxic + Reflect shells),
rather than continuing to prune within-species 3-of-4 similarities.

============================================================================
V73 — GENERATED-ONLY BIDE REBALANCE
============================================================================

Immutable source rule:
- Stadium rentals, player/tournament teams, historical builds, Smogon/source
  sets, RMTs, sample teams, and other externally documented sets were not altered.
- Only project-original / Red Rogue generated / retrofit sets were eligible.

Generated active sets containing Bide before pass: 115
Generated Bide sets safely adjusted: 63
Generated Bide sets intentionally left unchanged: 52

Replacement rule:
- preserve intended difficulty band
- use only moves already established on that exact species in project corpus
- avoid creating an exact duplicate
- penalize Body Slam / Reflect / Toxic / Thunder Wave as replacement fillers
- if no safe replacement exists, leave the set unchanged

Source-derived sets changed: 0
